paper.title_en: Inflation in $f(Q,\mathcal{L}_m)$ gravity: equivalence to $k$-inflation and ghost instabilities
paper.abstract_en: We study slow-roll inflation in $f(Q,\mathcal{L}_m)$ gravity, focusing on whether non-minimal matter--geometry couplings can support viable inflation. We show that the separable class linear in $Q$, $f(Q,\mathcal{L}_m)=-αQ+g(\mathcal{L}_m)$, is equivalent, up to a boundary term, to General Relativity minimally coupled to a $k$-essence scalar field. Thus, it introduces no additional gravitational degrees of freedom, and its inflationary predictions coincide with those of the corresponding $k$-inflation model. For the separable models considered, the observables depend on a single effective parameter combination, yielding a nonzero lower bound on the tensor-to-scalar ratio. While these models may marginally satisfy Planck 2018 constraints alone, they are strongly disfavored by the combined Planck 2018, baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO), and BICEP/Keck 2018 (BK18) constraints. This marginal agreement also requires a sizeable negative effective vacuum-energy contribution, driving the expanding background to $H=0$ shortly after inflation. For representative non-separable models with genuine $Q$-$\mathcal{L}_m$ couplings, including terms proportional to $γQV$ and $γQX$, we derive the quadratic perturbation action and find that two additional scalar degrees of freedom propagate on regular rolling backgrounds satisfying the relevant non-degeneracy conditions. Under these conditions, the kinetic matrix has at least one negative eigenvalue, indicating a ghost instability. Hence, background-level observational predictions alone cannot establish the physical viability of these models. Overall, for the classes considered, inflation in $f(Q,\mathcal{L}_m)$ gravity either reduces to $k$-inflation in General Relativity or exhibits ghost instabilities on regular, non-degenerate backgrounds.
